name: Big Thief
label: 4AD
lede: Two Berklee alumni and two friends lived on the road for years, then recorded an 80-minute double album in five studios during lockdown. Pitchfork ranked it No. 7 of 2022.

eras.title: Two songwriters, no band yet
eras.text: Adrianne Lenker was making solo records from her teens; Buck Meek was a Texas-born guitarist busking in New York subway stations. Both had passed through Berklee, and by 2013 they were touring as a duo.

years.src: Wikipedia: Adrianne Lenker
years.h: A first solo record, Stages of the Sun, from Adrianne Lenker
years.p: Wikipedia dates [[Adrianne Lenker|763cb144-afdb-471e-bd86-d4f5b9b58641]]'s discography to 2006, when the Minnesota-raised songwriter was around 15.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Stages of the Sun (2006) as the start of her discography, a decade before Big Thief's debut. She was homeschooled, got her GED at 16 and later went to Berklee College of Music on a scholarship from Susan Tedeschi, according to her Wikipedia biography.

years.src: Wikipedia: Big Thief · The Line of Best Fit
years.h: Lenker and Meek hit the road as a two-piece
years.p: Two guitars and two voices, working out the songs that would become Big Thief's.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Lenker and [[Buck Meek|b8780175-4ff4-4d87-8e54-999f70dbb5ec]] met at a show in Boston and reconnected in Brooklyn. Lenker told The Line of Best Fit she met Meek on her first day in New York, at 21. Either way, the duo toured in 2013, and in 2014 released two EPs, a-sides and b-sides.

years.h: Hours Were the Birds comes out twice, four years apart
years.p: Lenker self-released her second solo album in 2014; Saddle Creek reissued it in 2018, after Big Thief had made her name.

eras.title: Two albums for Saddle Creek, one van
eras.text: Big Thief became a band in 2015 and then mostly stopped having an address. They made two albums for Saddle Creek in just over a year and toured both until NPR and Spin noticed.

years.cap: Big Thief at SXSW, Austin, Texas
years.src: The Line of Best Fit · Wikipedia: Big Thief
years.h: The engineer becomes the drummer
years.p: James Krivchenia started out recording the album and ended up behind the kit; bassist Max Oleartchik, a Berklee friend of Buck Meek's, completed the four.
years.xp: According to The Line of Best Fit, Lenker and Meek bumped into Oleartchik on a New York street after about ten years. Jason Burger briefly played drums in 2015 (Wikipedia spells it Burger; the Line of Best Fit prints Berger) before Krivchenia, who had been engineering their record, took the kit.

years.src: Wikipedia: Masterpiece (Big Thief album) · The Line of Best Fit
years.h: A friend's great-aunt lends them a lake house for twelve days
years.p: The band cut Masterpiece in Essex, New York, on Lake Champlain, with [[Andrew Sarlo|700b0a0c-9c3b-44b3-8de4-51c1a5f4b2e1]] producing.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the sessions to July 1-12, 2015. The Line of Best Fit reports the album came out "untouched and unchanged," exactly as recorded. Sarlo, Lenker's friend from Berklee, went on to work on the band's records for years.

years.cap: Big Thief on stage at the Lexington, London
years.src: Wikipedia: Masterpiece (Big Thief album)
years.h: Masterpiece bets the debut on its own title
years.p: Saddle Creek released the 12-track record; Pitchfork gave it 7.7 and Metacritic averages 79 from 14 reviews.
years.xp: The cover is a photograph of Lenker's mother as a child, playing with a toy dinosaur. Wikipedia lists lovesickness, abuse and mental illness among its subjects, in songs that shift between lo-fi acoustic and loud, hooky rock.

years.src: NPR Music: Big Thief Tiny Desk Concert · Wikipedia: Big Thief
years.h: Big Thief play the NPR Tiny Desk, a few months after the debut
years.p: Recorded for NPR Music in August 2016, with Masterpiece out since May.
years.xp: NPR's page for the session is dated August 2016. NPR's Bob Boilen had already written that Big Thief were "a band bound by great songs," per Wikipedia.

years.cap: Big Thief performing at BSP, Kingston, New York, June 22, 2017
years.src: Wikipedia: Capacity (album) · Wikipedia: Big Thief
years.h: Capacity finishes 2017 at No. 2 on Spin's list
years.p: Recorded over a month in a house-sat farmhouse, it scored 8.3 at Pitchfork when it came out.
years.xp: "Mythological Beauty" premiered on NPR on April 4, 2017, and closing track "Mary" later landed at No. 44 on Pitchfork's 200 best songs of the 2010s. The cover is a photo of Lenker's uncle holding her as an infant. Sources differ on NPR's placement: Wikipedia's Big Thief page credits Boilen's personal top ten with it at No. 1, the Capacity page says No. 3.

eras.title: Woods first, then desert
eras.text: Signed to 4AD, the band recorded U.F.O.F. in the Washington woods and Two Hands in the Texas desert, releasing them five months apart. U.F.O.F. made them a Grammy-nominated band.

years.src: Wikipedia: Buck Meek · Wikipedia: U.F.O.F.
years.h: Lenker and Meek each release a solo album, and divorce
years.p: Lenker's Abysskiss came out on Saddle Creek and Meek's first solo record on Keeled Scales; Wikipedia says their marriage ended in 2018.
years.xp: Wikipedia's Meek page gives their marriage as 2012-2018. They stayed bandmates and collaborators. Two songs from Abysskiss, "From" and "Terminal Paradise," came back in different form on U.F.O.F.

years.src: The FADER: Big Thief escaped · Wikipedia: U.F.O.F.
years.h: Dom Monks sneaks the mics up and gets "Cattails" on the first take
years.p: The band recorded U.F.O.F. live in one big room at Bear Creek Studio in Woodinville, Washington, with Andrew Sarlo producing.
years.xp: Monks "sneaks mics up" rather than stopping the room, The FADER reported, so "Cattails" was already captured by the time the band finished playing it. The sessions came with a hot tub and a treehouse, and Lenker wrote "Century" on the grass at the studio. Drummer Krivchenia ran every track through a "Magic Box" of knobs, a kind of treatment unavailable on earlier records.

years.cap: Big Thief at The National's Homecoming festival, Cincinnati
years.src: Wikipedia: U.F.O.F. · Wikipedia: Big Thief
years.h: Pitchfork gives U.F.O.F. a 9.2 and Best New Music
years.p: It was their first record for 4AD; Metacritic averages 87, and three sold-out release shows ran May 2-5 in Los Angeles and Brooklyn.
years.xp: The title stands for "UFO friend." Pitchfork's Jeremy Larson called it "a mesmerizing flood of life filtered down into a concentrated drip," per Wikipedia. It later made Pitchfork's 200 best albums of the 2010s at No. 33.

years.big: "We didn't want to make a double album."
q: We didn't want to make a double album.
years.src: Stereogum: Big Thief's Big Year · Wikipedia: Big Thief
years.h: Two Hands, cut at Sonic Ranch in Tornillo, Texas
years.p: The studio sits about 30 miles from El Paso; the album arrived five months after U.F.O.F. as its raw, live counterpart.
years.xp: Lenker told Stereogum the two records were meant to contrast: U.F.O.F. ethereal and layered, Two Hands raw, live and plain. "We didn't want to make a double album, because we felt it was too dense," she said. Three years later they made one anyway.

years.h: A Grammy nomination for U.F.O.F., the band's first
years.p: Best Alternative Music Album. "Not" from Two Hands followed at the 2021 ceremony for Best Rock Song and Best Rock Performance.

eras.title: Lockdown and 45 songs
eras.text: With touring shut down, the band stayed put for the first time in five years. Lenker released her own records, and the band spent months building what became their biggest album.

years.h: Songs and Instrumentals: two solo records from Lenker on 4AD
years.p: Released in 2020, the year after Big Thief's two albums.

years.cap: Big Thief at Lisboa Ao Vivo, Lisbon, February 2020
years.src: Wikipedia: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You · Wikipedia: Big Thief
years.h: Lockdown sends the band through five studios in nine months
years.p: From April to December 2020 they recorded in Massachusetts, upstate New York, California, Colorado and Arizona, then cut 45 songs down to 20.
years.xp: Wikipedia's album page lists the Elf Inn (Westhampton, Massachusetts), Flying Cloud Recordings (upstate New York), Five Star Studios (Topanga), MusicGardens (Colorado) and Press On Studio (Tucson). Krivchenia produced; it was the first Big Thief record without Sarlo in the chair. Wikipedia's Big Thief page adds a two-week quarantine in the Vermont woods in July 2020.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You
years.h: "Little Things" goes out first, with "Sparrow"
years.p: Pitchfork named "Little Things" Best New Track, and it ranked No. 15 on the site's best songs of 2021.

years.h: "Certainty" follows as single number two
years.p: It would go on to a Grammy nomination for Best Alternative Music Performance.

years.cap: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You (4AD
years.h: "Change" makes three singles ahead of the album
years.p: Pitchfork later called the album a "20-song epic."
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Andy Cush called it "a 20-song epic of kaleidoscopic invention, striking beauty, and wigged-out humor," per Wikipedia. [[Mat Davidson|e4547aac-28f7-40f3-9a98-080034f3069d]] (Twain) plays fiddle and sings throughout, the first big fifth voice on a Big Thief record. Christgau gave it an A; AllMusic's 3.5 stars said it "lands much more like a showreel than a plotted album."

The 2022 singles ran from "Little Things" and "Certainty" through "Time Escaping," "No Reason" and "Simulation Swarm."

eras.title: The double album everyone ranked
eras.text: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You came out in February 2022 and landed near the top of year-end lists. The year also tested the band in public.

years.cap: Big Thief at the Barrowland Ballroom, Glasgow, February 25, 2022
years.src: Stereogum: Big Thief Cancel Tel Aviv Shows · Wikipedia: Big Thief
years.h: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You runs 20 songs and 80 minutes
years.p: [[James Krivchenia|611cb5a3-42cd-4aef-98e6-5749b88bf63a]] produced the 4AD double album; Pitchfork gave it 9.0 and ranked it No. 7 of 2022, and Metacritic averages 88.
years.xp: Stereogum reported that the first statement acknowledged the BDS movement, said the band did not claim to know where "the moral high ground lies," and pledged profits to Palestinian humanitarian groups. The reversal said they opposed the occupation and believed in "total freedom and self-determination for all Palestinians." The venue, Barby, posted an angry Hebrew response, and Consequence reported it called the band "cowards."

years.src: Consequence: Big Thief Happiness Tiny Desk
years.h: Big Thief book Tel Aviv, then cancel both shows
years.p: The band first said it wanted to play Oleartchik's hometown, then apologized for "the recklessness and naivete of our original statement" and pulled the July 6-7 dates.
years.xp: Stereogum reported that the first statement acknowledged the BDS movement, said the band did not claim to know where "the moral high ground lies," and pledged profits to Palestinian humanitarian groups. The reversal said they opposed the occupation and believed in "total freedom and self-determination for all Palestinians." The venue, Barby, posted an angry Hebrew response, and Consequence reported it called the band "cowards."

years.src: Consequence: Big Thief Happiness Tiny Desk
years.h: A second Tiny Desk, with a song nobody has heard
years.p: The July 2022 Home concert included "Happiness," unreleased at the time.

years.cap: Big Thief at Shepherd's Bush Empire, London, March 2, 2022
years.h: Dragon tops Paste's year-end list and takes No. 2 at The Atlantic
years.p: Pitchfork ranked it No. 7; Wikipedia also lists NPR Music at No. 4, Uncut at No. 5 and Rolling Stone at No. 35 of 100.

years.h: Dragon gets two Grammy nominations
years.p: Best Alternative Music Album for the record, plus Best Alternative Music Performance for "Certainty."

years.src: Wikipedia: Big Thief · Wikipedia: Double Infinity
years.h: Haunted Mountain is Meek's first solo record for 4AD
years.p: His third solo album, after Buck Meek (2018) and Two Saviors (2021).
years.xp: Wikipedia's Big Thief page dates his departure to June 2024; the Double Infinity page says July. The Portland show was the band's first in almost a year, with bassist Justin Felton and second percussionist Jon Nellen, and ten live debuts in a 14-song set.

eras.title: Three and a fraction
eras.text: Oleartchik left after nine years and the band chose not to replace him. They kept making records in bigger rooms with more guests, and they are active.

years.cap: Adrianne Lenker playing solo at the Barbican, London, April 2024
years.src: Wikipedia: Double Infinity
years.h: Lenker's Bright Future earns a Best Folk Album nomination
years.p: Her 2024 solo album on 4AD; Wikipedia counts five Grammy nominations for her overall.
years.xp: Rather than hire a bassist, Lenker, Meek and Krivchenia invited ten session players, including [[Laraaji|249e0ab9-2690-47f3-8c9a-ef7bb62ee466]]. Lenker said the band "can expand and contract." Metacritic averages 84, and Mojo ranked it No. 4 of 2025.

years.src: JamBase: Big Thief Horsepower
years.h: Oleartchik steps off the bass after nine years
years.p: The band cited "interpersonal reasons"; on July 28 they played Project Pabst in Portland with a five-piece lineup.
years.xp: Per JamBase, the triple album was recorded in Nashville in May 2026 and played in non-sequential order; both nights, August 22-23, were professionally filmed. Lenker and Meek said the album is targeted for spring 2027.

years.src: Wikipedia: Double Infinity
years.h: Big Thief make Double Infinity without a bassist
years.p: Recorded in three weeks at Power Station in New York with producer Dom Monks, it drew a 7.6 from Pitchfork.
years.xp: Rather than hire a bassist, Lenker, Meek and Krivchenia invited session players including [[Laraaji|249e0ab9-2690-47f3-8c9a-ef7bb62ee466]]. Lenker said the band "can expand and contract." Metacritic averages 84, and Mojo ranked it No. 4 of 2025.

years.p: A table onstage, and guests including [[Lucinda Williams|21685b15-3074-446e-aa1d-ff7157014f53]], Gillian Welch, Iris DeMent and Rodney Crowell.
